facts.raw_span: A 66-year-old man presented with a 24-hour history of incomplete closure of the right eye
flattening of the right nasolabial fold
right-sided hemiplegia rendering him unable to sit up or stand
The patient had a 3-year history of hypertension
no history of neurological disorders
The patient was alert and oriented
Effacement of the right frontal wrinkle
Incomplete closure of the right eyelid
Muscle strength in the right upper and lower extremities: grade 0/5
Hypoesthesia noted on the right side
Right Babinski sign: positive
Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle at 24 hours postonset

concepts.why: The patient presented with right-sided hemiplegia, muscle strength grade 0/5, and a positive Babinski sign, which are consistent with a left-sided intracerebral hemorrhage, as confirmed by the CT scan showing hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and lateral ventricle.
The CT scan specifically showed hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region, which is consistent with a thalamic hemorrhage.
The patient had a 3-year history of hypertension, which is a risk factor for intracerebral hemorrhage, and the CT scan confirmed the presence of a hemorrhage.
The patient presented with sudden onset of right-sided hemiplegia, which is a common symptom of a stroke, and the presence of a hemorrhage on the CT scan confirms the diagnosis.

The patient presented with muscle strength grade 0/5 and a positive Babinski sign, which are consistent with a lesion affecting the corticospinal tract, as seen in the diffusion tensor imaging showing a thinner corticobulbar tract on the left side.

rationales.F01: Incomplete closure of the right eye suggests a cranial nerve VII lesion, which could be due to a stroke or intracerebral hemorrhage.
rationales.F03: Right-sided hemiplegia is a strong indicator of a corticospinal tract lesion, which could be due to a stroke or intracerebral hemorrhage.
rationales.F09: Muscle strength grade 0/5 in the right upper and lower extremities indicates a severe motor deficit, consistent with a corticospinal tract lesion.
rationales.F11: A positive Babinski sign is a strong indicator of an upper motor neuron lesion, which could be due to a stroke or intracerebral hemorrhage.
rationales.F12: Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region is a strong indicator of a thalamic hemorrhage, which is a type of intracerebral hemorrhage.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies, particularly the hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region, most strongly support thalamic hemorrhage as the diagnosis.
